title: weeklyOSM 852
content:
12/11/2026-18/11/2026

  • Voting has started on the crossing cleanup and deprecation proposal and is open until 2 December 2026. The proposal aims to formally approve crossing:signals=* and deprecate most uses of crossing=* in favour of separate tags for crossing signals and markings. The values crossing=no and crossing=informal would remain in use.

The values crossing=no and crossing=informal would remain in use.

  • Baprischka has proposed a new tag, tomb=loculi, for walls fitted with burial niches (loculi), which are particularly common in Italian cemeteries. The tag should only be used on lines, with the niches situated to the right of the line’s direction. So far, only `tomb=columbarium` exists for buildings with niches inside; alternatively, this tag could also be used on lines. The community has been discussing the proposal on the OSM Community forum since 12 November.

title: weeklyOSM 851
content:
05/11/2026-11/11/2026

  • Telegram Sam proposed tagging seaplane bases with aeroway=seaplane_base instead of aeroway=aerodrome, as they have no runways or aprons and more closely resemble harbours. The water landing area should use seamark:type=seaplane_landing_area instead of aeroway=runway, while landuse=industrial with industrial=port prevents retagged bases from disappearing from maps. The discussion is ongoing in the forum.

    • MaggieMaps and Jake Low are proposing to describe wetlands using the new keys wetland:connectivity, wetland:vegetation, and wetland:landform to specify their water source, vegetation, and terrain position, and extending the use of salt=* and anthropogenic=yes to wetlands. OpenStreetMap US is working with the Environmental Policy Innovation Center on OpenWetlandsMap, an OSM-based dataset. The discussion is ongoing on the Wiki and in the OpenStreetMap US Slack.

  • Rphyrin used osm_pantau to highlight where mappers participated in the HOT Global Solidarity Mapathon 1 on Friday 6 November 2026.

  • Rtnf has noticed a growing trend of new tools bringing the Wikidata and OpenStreetMap ecosystems closer together.

title: weeklyOSM 850
content:
29/10/2026-04/11/2026

  • The iD tagging schema v7.3.0 was released, bringing new features to iD, GoMap!!, EveryDoor, and other editors. It includes several new, better icons. A number of new structural definitions are now available for editing software. Presets now state, for example, that nodes within power=line are more likely to be power=tower than, for example, waterway=waterfall. Information about more relation roles was also added. Note that editing software needs to be updated to use this new info. Also included were many other improvements, new presets for railway=platform_edge and more. Many icon improvements, bugfixes, tweaks and documentation improvements. 151 changes in total. Thanks to all contributors!
  • Tykayn is inviting people on Mastodon to contribute to the France Project of the Month (Projet du Mois) on schools . There are 9,900 schools left to be added to OSM in the France metropolitan area, and 45,000 schools have been recorded by OSM contributors since the project began in 2025.

title: weeklyOSM 849
content:
22/10/2026-28/10/2026

  • Andy Mabbett has proposed a tagging scheme for the concrete arrows and illuminated beacon towers along the historic US Transcontinental Airway System. These physical navigation aids were built to guide early airmail pilots. Concrete arrows were enormous arrows painted or laid out on the ground, often on hilltops or open land, pointing pilots towards the next route segment. Beacon towers were tall structures equipped with powerful lights that helped pilots follow the route at night.

title: weeklyOSM 847
content:
08/10/2026-14/10/2026

  • Two tagging proposals, related to graffiti, are open for voting until 26 October 2026. Evyy is proposing a dedicated tag, shop=graffiti, for shops specialising in spray cans, markers, stickers, and other street art supplies, which have often been tagged as shop=craft or shop=paint in the past. Flappiegrrr is proposing to use leisure=graffiti_wall to record places where graffiti may be sprayed legally, and to describe individual walls using the key graffiti_wall=*.

  • [1] Altilunium has developed ‘Know Your Mapper’, a web app that explores an OSM mapper’s editing sessions and approximate areas of activity.

    • [1] Altilunium has developed ‘Know Your Mapper’, a web app that explores an OSM mapper’s editing sessions and approximate areas of activity.

  • The small team behind OpenClimbing: Jan Václavík, Pavel Zbytovský, and Fabian Weisshaar, have created their second bot proposal to clean up climbing-related tags in OpenStreetMap. Running with assistance from Mateusz Konieczny, the bot aims to improve the consistency and quality of OSM climbing data. OpenClimbing uses this information to power its specialised map with integrated topos for the climbing community.

title: weeklyOSM 845
content:
24/09/2026-30/09/2026

  • We’re excited to announce that weeklyOSM is now accessible via news.osm.org, honouring the voices and contributions of our global community equally. The new domain redirects to weeklyOSM.eu.
  • Eugene Alvin Villar announced the #31DayOSMChallenge proposed by the OpenStreetMap Foundation’s Local Chapters and Communities Working Group. See the Daily Challenges and note that you don’t have to contribute every day.

  • Raquel Dezidério Souto wrote, in her OSM User Diary, that she has edited two new volumes of the book Case Studies in Collaborative and Participatory Mapping (one of which is a thematic dossier on risk and disaster reduction). She authored chapters on the application of OpenStreetMap in two case studies conducted in collaboration with the Brazilian Ministry of Integration and Regional Development (part of volume 2). In total, 35 chapters were published, and the two e-books are available as open access on the Editora IVIDES portal.

title: weeklyOSM 844
content:
17/09/2026-23/09/2026

  • Next week we will launch our completely revamped website; an exciting milestone for us! With Hugo as our new framework, a self-hosted commenting system (Remark42), and our own Listmonk server for managing mailing lists, we’ve modernised our publishing workflow and automated key processes. The source code is available, along with the complete archive in Markdown format, in the FOSSGIS GitLab repository. Cross your fingers for a smooth transition.
  • [1] After almost 15 years, mappers in the US state of Ohio have finished mapping the boundaries of all 1,309 townships there. The community overcame a lack of accurate, authoritative, external datasets by reconciling a variety of sources. Work remains to clean up and update municipal boundaries, which often influence township boundaries.

  • Walid Nouh has interviewed members of the OpenStreetMap France board on the Projets Libres podcast. The episode’s guests were asked to talk about OSM-FR, who they are, what the association does, and its current activities.

title: weeklyOSM 843
content:
10/09/2026-16/09/2026

  • v7.2.0 of the iD tagging schema has been released and includes tweaks to labels, new icons, changed fields for various presets, new search terms, better documentation, improved build scripts, and more. Helper presets for some subvariants of aerialway stations, silos, and parking spots were added to make mapping easier. An actual new preset was added for offshore platforms. It includes bugfixes such as dropping bad suggestions, taginfo report includes addTags, and post boxes in USA no longer have duplicate drivethrough fields. Work continues in the background on some larger features, but changes listed above will soon be present in iD, GoMap!!, EveryDoor, StreetComplete, and other editors.

  • Andy Allan gave a talk at State of the Map 2026 about how OpenStreetMap’s transport layer migrated from server-side rendered map tiles to client-side rendered vector styles.
